text:
Priya (AE): Quick sync - Greenline POC reporting frequent websocket disconnects through their edge proxy. They use our Rust SDK and see sessions drop after ~90s idle. Asking for recommended keepalive, if keepalive counts as tokens, and whether short-lived creds (5m) are ok for their connector refresh loop.

Aisha (Solutions): Short answer: use WS ping or TCP keepalive. Those do NOT count as model token usage. Only actual inference/generation RPCs consume tokens. If possible, bump proxy idle beyond 90s.

Ben (Runtime Eng): Confirmed. WS ping frames are handled at transport layer and won't enter the batching/serving path. Two caveats: 1) Dedicated infra sometimes enforces aggressive idle teardown (~2m) depending on cluster config; 2) reconnects that re-run the full context warmup will incur token cost.

Priya (AE): Ok—so pings are free. If they add client pings every 25s will that affect our batching heuristics or billing?

Ben (Runtime Eng): No effect on batching or billing. Batching happens for incoming generation requests at the API layer. Transport-level keepalives are orthogonal. If they send tiny generation calls as keepalive, that would hit batching and cost tokens - avoid that.

Marco (Presales): They also asked about ephemeral key cadence. They plan to mint 5m keys per connector lifecycle. Is that supported operationally?

Aisha (Solutions): 5m is supported but tight. We typically recommend 15m for POCs to avoid refresh storms. If they insist on 5m, implement jittered refresh and exponential backoff on failures. Provide sample flow:

Priya (AE): Can you paste a concise Rust snippet and a sample curl for token refresh we can share?

Aisha (Solutions): Sure — Rust pseudo: 
```rust
// tokio-tungstenite ws ping example
ws_stream.send(Message::Ping(vec![])).await?; // keepalive, no token cost
socket.set_keepalive(Some(Duration::from_secs(25))); // tcp keepalive
```
And refresh exchange example: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/auth/refresh \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <refresh-token>" \\
  -d '{"scope":"inference"}'
```
Add 10-30s jitter to refresh schedule.

deploy-bot: Note: Request made to eng-runtime to review Dedicated cluster idle policy for a temporary POC extension.

Ben (Runtime Eng): Also flag: if their connector recreates model state on every reconnect (e.g., re-send long system prompts to re-warm KV cache), they will pay for that re-gen. Recommend snapshotting minimal state server-side or using a local checkpoint to rehydrate without full re-generation.

Priya (AE): Pricing question from customer: is a POC always PAYG or can we do a short reserved trial to cap costs?

Marco (Presales): Default is PAYG. For predictable, sustained load during evals we can offer a short reserved commit—send me estimated QPS and expected hours and I can draft a short trial pricing note.

Aisha (Solutions): Summary for handoff: 1) Use WS ping/TCP keepalive; 2) Avoid noop generation calls; 3) 5m ephemeral creds supported but 15m recommended; 4) Add jittered refresh; 5) Consider local checkpointing to avoid re-warm costs; 6) Engage eng-runtime if you need temporary cluster idle policy changes. I can turn this into a one-page checklist.

Priya (AE): Please do the checklist. I'll attach to POC handoff doc and ask Greenline for proxy logs. Thanks everyone :pray:
